title: Turkiye's domestic producer price index rises 27.38% in September 2026
summary:
Turkiye's D-PPI rose 27.38 per cent year on year and 2.07 per cent month on month in September 2026, on a 2003=100 base.
Manufactured products increased 29.09 per cent annually and 2.32 per cent monthly, Turkish Statistical Institute data showed.
Energy led main industrial groups with a 30.82 per cent annual rise and 3.55 per cent monthly gain.

title: ASF stable with upstream ACN, propylene: What next for acrylic fibre?
summary:
Prices of acrylic staple fibre (ASF), acrylonitrile (ACN) and propylene in China and wider Asia stayed stable from September 28 to October 2, 2026.
Against August 2 levels, ASF was 2.6 per cent higher, propylene rose by up to 18.8 per cent and ACN was 8.8 per cent lower.
Propylene had advanced before September 28 with crude and then consolidated at a higher plateau.

title: India specialty fibres rise 2-3%: Is the premium gap widening?
summary:
India's specialty cellulosic fibre complex saw all eight specialty SKUs reprice on October 1 during September 28–October 2, then hold levels through Friday.
Ecovero rose 2.94–3.23 per cent, Liva Eco 2.14–2.36 per cent and Modal 2.22–2.41 per cent.
Most standard benchmarks in China, India and Pakistan were flat, widening selected specialty-to-standard fibre spreads by 5–10 per cent.

title: Vietnam posts $1.27 bn trade surplus in September 2026
summary:
Vietnam recorded a $1.27 billion merchandise trade surplus in September, ending nine straight months of deficit, the National Statistics Office said.
Trade turnover reached $117.69 billion in the month, up 7.3 per cent month-on-month and 42.4 per cent year-on-year.
First-nine-month trade still showed a $19.42 billion deficit as imports rose faster than exports.

title: India's economy to grow 7.1% in FY27: World Bank
summary:
India’s economy is projected to grow 7.1 per cent in FY27, supported by domestic demand and exports, the World Bank said. 
Medium-term prospects remained strong despite risks from oil prices, El Niño and market corrections.
Private AI investment rose to $4.1 billion in 2025, while the bank urged stronger infrastructure, wider access and workforce development to ensure broadly shared AI benefits.

title: Indian cabinet approves $1.04 bn SME Growth Fund
summary:
India’s Cabinet has approved a ₹10,000 crore (~$1.04 billion) government commitment to set up the SME Growth Fund for direct equity investments in small and medium enterprises.
The fund targets a gap in long-term growth capital, with majority allocation for manufacturing-focused SMEs.
It will also consider SMEs in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities.

title: MEG falls 3.85% as PTA, PX rise: Why polyester costs are not falling?
summary:
MEG CFR China fell 3.85 per cent to $750/mt between September 28 and October 2, but firmer PTA and PX limited polyester cost relief across Asia.
PX CFR Southeast Asia rose 0.38 per cent and PTA CFR Far East Asia gained 1.06 per cent, while Brent crude declined 2.88 per cent.
TexPro said buyers should monitor MEG and PTA separately before purchases, with PTA CFR India unchanged at $1,040/mt.

title: EU & euro area producer prices rise 1.9% in August
summary:
Industrial producer prices rose 1.9 per cent month on month in both the euro area and the EU in August 2026, Eurostat first estimates showed.
Annual increases reached 8.2 per cent in the euro area and 8.0 per cent in the EU.
Energy prices rose 5.6 per cent in the euro area and 5.5 per cent in the EU month on month, while all Member States recorded increases.

title: Cotton yarn prices dip in south India, but optimism persists
summary:
South Indian cotton yarn prices remained under pressure as weak downstream demand and lower ICE cotton pushed Mumbai and Tiruppur lower.
Mumbai yarn fell ₹3–7 (~$0.03–0.07) per kg and Tiruppur dropped ₹2–3 per kg as mills adjusted rates; traders saw scope for buying to improve after inventories reduced.
Gujarat cotton recovered ₹500 per candy despite rising new-season arrivals and high-moisture Kapas.

title: Thermore partners with Patagonia for Heyes Peak collection
summary:
Thermore partnered with Patagonia to supply EVOdown insulation for five men’s and women’s Heyes Peak styles.
Made entirely from recycled PET bottle fibres, the insulation offers warmth, softness and easy care.
The collection’s jacket pairs EVOdown with recycled fishing-net nylon and a water-repellent finish without intentionally added PFAS. All styles are made in a Fair Trade Certified factory.

title: Japan's Sanyo Shokai maintains FY27 profit plan after H1 loss
summary:
Japan's Sanyo Shokai maintained its FY27 plan despite a wider H1 loss, targeting ¥60 billion (~$379.79 million sales). 
H1 net sales fell 4 per cent YoY to ¥25.95 billion (~$164.26 million); operating loss widened and gross margin slipped to 60.4 per cent. 
Recovery rests on 11 per cent September retail sales growth, tighter markdowns, full-price selling and e-commerce expansion.

title: $5,059 freight gap meets tariffs: What really decides Asian sourcing?
summary:
Asian apparel sourcing is being reshaped by a $5,059 per FEU gap between routes to the US West Coast and North Europe, enough to erase narrow FOB advantages.
January-July 2026 data show China, India and Vietnam fared better in Europe, while Cambodia grew 10.9 per cent in the US despite higher freight.
Tariffs, EU preferences, product mix, lead times and Suez risk now decide competitiveness.

title: BrilliA buys majority stake in Malaysian lingerie brand Neubodi
summary:
BrilliA has acquired a majority equity interest in Malaysian lingerie brand and speciality retailer Neubodi, effective August 1, 2026.
The deal moves the intimate apparel service provider beyond B2B supply and design into consumer-facing speciality retail in Southeast Asia.
Neubodi adds 11 stores, e-commerce and social channels; management targets about $3 million in 2026 net sales.

title: Cambodia’s $212 wage: Who wins, who loses and fight behind the figure
summary:
Cambodia has set a $212 monthly minimum wage for garment, textile, footwear and travel-goods workers from January 1, 2027, up $2 from $210.
Workers had sought $225 after unions earlier demanded $250.66; employers wanted to retain $210 with a temporary $2.50 allowance.
The sector employs nearly one million workers and exported $11.76 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up 7.2 per cent.

title: RMG exports from Bangladesh grow 6% in Q1 2026-27
summary:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports grew 6.10 per cent to $10.578 billion in July-September 2026, Export Promotion Bureau data showed.
Knitwear rose 6.88 per cent to $5.963 billion, while woven apparel increased 5.11 per cent to $4.416 billion.
Home textiles gained 11.94 per cent to $231.29 million, but cotton and cotton products fell 12.41 per cent to $125.11 million.

title: Africa’s 1.69 bn SME US apparel window: What’s holding it back?
summary:
AGOA’s 2026-27 apparel ceiling is 1.6908 billion SME, but special-rule use was only 41.48 per cent by September 15, 2025.
TexPro shows Africa exported $13.27 billion of apparel in 2025; HS61 and HS62 exports rose only around 0.6 per cent in January-May 2026.
The main gap is textile capacity: spinning, knitting, weaving, dyeing, finishing, trims, washing and reliable utilities.

title: Bangladesh’s apparel industry and the changing fabric equation
summary:
Bangladesh exported an estimated $38.825 billion worth of apparel in 2025, but 76.94 per cent of its export basket came from basic categories.
A September 2026 amendment to the Import Policy Order 2026–2029 has eased access to specialised fabrics for specified apparel categories.
The change could support sportswear, functional apparel, MMF-based products and wider product diversification.

title: Sri Lanka’s apparel sector and the $3 bn growth challenge
summary:
Sri Lanka aims to lift merchandise exports from around $13.6 billion in 2025 to $28 billion by 2030, with textiles and apparel a key contributor.
The sector generates about $5 billion annually, over a third of merchandise export earnings, and targets $8 billion by 2030.
Growth hinges on domestic supply chains, productivity, value addition, higher-value products and market access.

title: Sri Lanka's garment exports dip to $3.3 bn in Jan-Aug
summary:
Sri Lanka's garment exports fell 6.3 per cent to $3,108.3 million in January-August 2026.
Textile exports declined 9.4 per cent to $177.6 million; other manufactured textile articles eased 14.2 per cent to $69.7 million.
Total textile product exports formed 45.78 per cent of industrial exports, while textile and textile article imports fell 4.5 per cent to $1,713.2 million.

title: Marks & Spencer backs UK textile recycling chain built to scale
summary:
UK generated around 1.4 million tonnes of post-consumer textiles in 2024, with nearly half estimated non-reusable.
M&S, New Look, Sainsbury's Tu Clothing and Oxfam have joined Circle-8's The Circuit to build a collection, sorting and pre-processing supply chain.
Phase one starts in January 2027 at Oxfam's Batley site, testing automated sorting, traceability and recycler links.
